title: Cholesky optimized via buffer_cleanup
text:
Kernel: Cholesky (group=linalg)
Angle applied: buffer_cleanup
Speedup: 1.07x (12479 → 11702 cycles)
What changed:
P1: Several module-scope DSDs that were never reassigned (`col_buf_dsd`, `row_buf_dsd`, `col_in`) were promoted from `var` to `const`. In the `cont` task, the per-iteration `var invsqrt` was made `const`, and dead comment blocks were dropped. The interior-block branch's trailing tile_dsd reset now uses a single `@increment_dsd_offset` with a negative stride instead of rebuilding a fresh `mem1d_dsd` via `@get_dsd`.

P2: Under buffer_cleanup, eliminating mutable storage for DSD descriptors lets the compiler keep them in registers and skip reload/spill traffic across the task boundary, and removing the redundant `@get_dsd` rebuild avoids re-materializing the tile base descriptor each cont() invocation. Combined with the const-folded `invsqrt`, these shave setup cycles on the hot interior-PE path, dropping cycles_send from 12479 to 11702.

title: Cholesky optimized via comptime_value_tuning
text:
Kernel: Cholesky (group=linalg)
Angle applied: comptime_value_tuning
Speedup: 1.07x (12479 → 11653 cycles)
What changed:
P1: Promoted several mutable `var` DSD bindings (`col_buf_dsd`, `row_buf_dsd`, `col_in`) and the `invsqrt` scalar in the `cont` task to `const`. Converted two runtime `for (@range(u16, Nt))` loops in the `cont` task (the diagonal `tile_row` `@fmacs` loop and the interior-block `tile_dsd` `@fmacs` loop) into `inline for (@range(i16, Nt))` loops, with a corresponding `@as(u16, i+1)` cast on `@set_dsd_length`.

P2: Under comptime_value_tuning, marking DSDs `const` lets the compiler bake fabric/queue descriptors and memory strides as compile-time immediates instead of reloading mutable DSD state per use. The `inline for` over the comptime-known `Nt` unrolls the per-row `@fmacs` chain, eliminating loop-counter compare/branch overhead and letting `@increment_dsd_offset` and `@set_dsd_length` fold into constant offsets, shaving the ~826 cycles observed.

title: Cholesky optimized via OPEN
text:
Kernel: Cholesky (group=linalg)
Angle applied: OPEN
Speedup: 1.07x (12479 → 11702 cycles)
What changed:
[OPEN-MODE HYPOTHESIS] On the diagonal-PE cont() path (px==py, non-fringe), the current code uses a scalar @range loop with a growing triangular fmacs (length i+1) and reissues `tile_row = @increment_dsd_offset(..., Nt, f32)` every iteration. The trailing send `@mov32(col_out, row_buf_dsd, ...)` happens AFTER this serial triangular update completes, so the column send is fully serialized behind compute. Hoist the column send to start BEFORE the triangular update so the async fabric mov32 overlaps with the local fmacs work — the diagonal PE's downstream column consumers can begin earlier, shortening the critical path on every non-fringe step of every column.

Hoist the row send to start IMMEDIATELY after the fmuls scaling completes (before the trailing-update fmacs loop), so the async row mov32 overlaps with the local fmacs work on every left-edge step. The fmacs loop reads tile_dsd (the scaled column) for the multiplicand but updates a DIFFERENT slice (dest_col_dsd starting at ti+1), so concurrent async readout of tile_dsd is safe.

title: Laplacian2D-Halo optimized via comptime_cleanup
text:
Kernel: Laplacian2D-Halo (group=stencil)
Angle applied: comptime_cleanup
Speedup: 1.48x (1709 → 1156 cycles)
What changed:
[ACCEPTED VIA REPAIR ATTEMPT 1] P1: The scalar `while` loop that staged the east/west boundary columns into `col_send_{e,w}` was replaced by two strided `mem1d_dsd` views into `tile` (`tile_col_w_dsd`, `tile_col_e_dsd`) driven by single `@fmovs` calls inside an `extract_columns` helper. The scalar `while` that copied `new_tile` back into `tile` was likewise replaced by one `@fmovs` over a pair of length-`MN` `mem1d_dsd`s. Comptime constants `MN` and `QUARTER` were hoisted.

P2: Under `comptime_cleanup`, folding `Mt*Nt` into the comptime constant `MN` and lifting the staging/copy loops into DSD-driven `@fmovs` removes per-iteration loop overhead (index increment, compare, branch, address recompute) that the SEND path incurred each call. The hardware streams the strided column extraction and the bulk tile copy as single DSD operations, collapsing dozens of scalar instructions into one issue each, which directly shrinks the measured `cycles_send` window from 1709 to 1156.

title: Laplacian2D-Halo optimized via stride_optimization
text:
Kernel: Laplacian2D-Halo (group=stencil)
Angle applied: stride_optimization
Speedup: 1.13x (1081 → 959 cycles)
What changed:
P1: The scalar `while` loop that copied tile columns into `col_send_{w,e}` was replaced by two `@fmovs` calls over strided `mem1d_dsd`s (`tile_col_w_dsd`, `tile_col_e_dsd` with stride `Nt`) into the contiguous `col_send_*_dsd`s, wrapped in an `extract_columns()` helper. The send task now invokes that helper instead of the per-`i` scalar loads/stores, and comptime constants (`MN`, `MN_MINUS_NT`, `NT_MINUS_1`) replace recomputed index expressions.

P2: Under `stride_optimization`, the column staging is exactly the work measured by `cycles_send`. The old loop issued `Mt` separate scalar loads with multiply-based index math (`i*Nt`) and `Mt` scalar stores per side. The strided `mem1d_dsd` collapses each column into one hardware-iterated DSD op whose address generator advances by `Nt` per element with no loop overhead or index recomputation, cutting the staging from ~`Mt` scalar iterations to two pipelined DSD moves.

title: Laplacian2D-Halo optimized via circbuf_save_address
text:
Kernel: Laplacian2D-Halo (group=stencil)
Angle applied: circbuf_save_address
Speedup: 1.07x (730 → 680 cycles)
What changed:
P1: The scalar column-staging loop in `f_send` was replaced by `@fmovs` calls over strided `mem1d_dsd`s (`tile_col_w_dsd`, `tile_col_e_dsd`) into `col_send_{w,e}_dsd`, factored into an `extract_columns()` fn. The async fabric send `@fmovs` calls themselves are unchanged in shape, queue, and color, preserving the SEND task's externally visible behavior and DSD extents.

P2: Under `circbuf_save_address`, SEND-side cycles are dominated by per-wavelet bookkeeping for the column staging plus issuing fabric ops. Replacing the per-element `while` loop with two strided `@fmovs` lets the DSD hardware stream `Mt` elements without re-saving loop/address state each iteration, collapsing the staging cost into two bulk descriptor issues. That removes ~50 cycles of loop overhead inside the SEND task, lowering cycles_send from 730 to 680.

title: Laplacian2D-Halo optimized via OPEN
text:
Kernel: Laplacian2D-Halo (group=stencil)
Angle applied: OPEN
Speedup: 1.01x (680 → 671 cycles)
What changed:
[OPEN-MODE HYPOTHESIS] Fuse the stencil compute with the copy-back: instead of writing the 4 contributions into new_tile then doing a separate @fmovs to copy new_tile back into tile, write the final result directly into tile in place. Specifically, since after the stencil completes we overwrite tile entirely with new_tile, we can compute new values directly into tile by first scaling the up-contribution into a temp pattern but actually — better: build the result into new_tile and then SWAP pointers logically by alternating which buffer is "current". But the host reads `new_tile`, so we must end with the final result in new_tile. The cheapest win: eliminate the full-tile @fmovs copy-back by doing the stencil read from `tile` and write to `new_tile`, then for the next iteration swap roles via reading the previously-written buffer. Since iters=1 in the test, the copy-back is pure overhead — skip it entirely when remaining_iters==1, and only do it (or swap) on multi-iter runs. For iters==1 this eliminates the entire copy_new_to_tile pass.

title: GEMM_Collectives_2D optimized via per_row_dsd_unroll
text:
Kernel: GEMM_Collectives_2D (group=gemm)
Angle applied: per_row_dsd_unroll
Speedup: 1.45x (51738 → 35794 cycles)
What changed:
P1: The compute task now builds two base `mem1d_dsd` descriptors once (an `A_base` over a length-Mt column and a `C_base` over a length-Mt column of `C_tile`) instead of recreating `C_dsd` inside the outer loop and mutating both DSDs via `@increment_dsd_offset` per iteration. The inner `for` over `Nt` becomes an `inline for`, and each iteration derives `A_col`/`C_col` by a comptime-offset `@increment_dsd_offset` before issuing one `@fmacs`.

P2: Under per_row_dsd_unroll, the inner-loop trip counter, branch, and the runtime `@increment_dsd_offset` updates on `C_dsd`/`A_dsd` are eliminated: the `inline for` over Nt expands into a straight-line sequence of `@fmacs` whose DSD offsets (`j*Mt`, `k*Mt`) are comptime constants folded into descriptor setup. This removes loop overhead and serial dependency on the mutated DSD, letting the Kt outer iterations issue back-to-back fmacs, cutting cycles_send from 51738 to 35794.

title: Game_of_Life optimized via OPEN
text:
Kernel: Game_of_Life (group=all)
Angle applied: OPEN
Speedup: 1.05x (7838 → 7461 cycles)
What changed:
[OPEN-MODE HYPOTHESIS] Eliminate the sync_fwd hop: instead of waiting for E/W sends to drain before allowing the fwd_east_west task, chain the fwd_east_west activation directly off the second E/W send's async completion (via .unblock/.activate on send_east/send_west in the send task), and have the recv_north/recv_south tasks just @unblock fwd_east_west when both N/S have arrived. This removes one task hop (sync_fwd) per generation from the critical path and uses the same async-completion mechanism already in place for sync_send.

title: Game_of_Life optimized via OPEN
text:
Kernel: Game_of_Life (group=all)
Angle applied: OPEN
Speedup: 1.01x (7461 → 7407 cycles)
What changed:
[OPEN-MODE HYPOTHESIS] Eliminate the sync_send task hop entirely on the critical path. Currently fwd_east_west issues async E/W sends whose completion fires sync_send, which then @unblocks send_task to start the next generation. But send_task is also blocked at the start of a generation until recvs come in; we don't actually need to wait for fwd E/W sends to drain before re-arming send_task — we just need to wait before starting the next generation's E/W sends. Since the next generation's E/W sends go on the same queues, the hardware will serialize them naturally after the forward sends drain. So we can have fwd_east_west just unblock send_task directly (no async-completion hop, no sync_send task at all), removing one task activation per generation from the critical path.

title: Game_of_Life optimized via OPEN
text:
Kernel: Game_of_Life (group=all)
Angle applied: OPEN
Speedup: 1.07x (7407 → 6946 cycles)
What changed:
[OPEN-MODE HYPOTHESIS] Eliminate the sync_fwd task hop entirely by chaining the second E/W async send's completion to directly @activate fwd_east_west (instead of activating sync_fwd which then calls maybe_activate_fwd). The "both prerequisites met" gate becomes: N/S recvs @unblock fwd_east_west, and the last E/W send @activate's it. Combined with @block(fwd_east_west_task_id) initially, this removes one task dispatch per generation from the critical path. The fwd_ready_count logic is replaced by the implicit block/unblock+activate handshake.

title: Game_of_Life optimized via OPEN
text:
Kernel: Game_of_Life (group=all)
Angle applied: OPEN
Speedup: 1.05x (6946 → 6641 cycles)
What changed:
[OPEN-MODE HYPOTHESIS] Eliminate the fwd_east_west task entirely by forwarding N/S neighbor values inline from within the recv_north/recv_south tasks themselves: as soon as a N (or S) value arrives, immediately issue an async E/W fmovs of that single value (scalar broadcast) using a 1-element fabout DSD. The hardware output queues already serialize these forward sends behind the next generation's E/W sends, so we preserve ordering. This removes one task hop (fwd_east_west) plus its associated @block/@unblock/@activate bookkeeping from the critical path of every generation, while keeping the same data on the wire.

title: Game_of_Life optimized via OPEN
text:
Kernel: Game_of_Life (group=all)
Angle applied: OPEN
Speedup: 1.01x (6641 → 6546 cycles)
What changed:
[OPEN-MODE HYPOTHESIS] Eliminate the start_next_gen task hop entirely by inlining its work into whichever recv task observes num_recv == num_neighbors. The completing recv already has current_sum and val in registers; computing the next state, advancing the DSD, resetting counters, unblocking the recv tasks, and re-activating send directly from that recv saves one task dispatch (and the @activate latency) per generation. For 20 generations on the critical PE this removes ~20 task-hop overheads from the measured interval.

title: Game_of_Life optimized via OPEN
text:
Kernel: Game_of_Life (group=all)
Angle applied: OPEN
Speedup: 1.05x (6546 → 6261 cycles)
What changed:
[OPEN-MODE HYPOTHESIS] Eliminate the per-generation `state_dsd = @increment_dsd_offset(...)` update in the hot path by sending directly from the scalar `states[current_iter]` value: replace the four async `@fmovs(send_*_dsd, state_dsd, ...)` calls in `send()` and the two forward sends in `recv_north`/`recv_south` with single-wavelet sends sourced from a small scratch buffer that's written once per generation. More importantly, remove the `@increment_dsd_offset` work and use direct array indexing into `states[current_iter]` via a precomputed value held in a 1-element scratch `cur` array whose DSD is built once at comptime — this saves the DSD-offset update plus reduces register pressure on the recv-completion path. Additionally, combine `num_recv == num_neighbors` check by precomputing the comparison threshold as a const and dropping the redundant `num_west_recv`/`num_east_recv` counters by using `num_recv` plus a single per-side counter folded into the same compare when possible — but the main win is killing the DSD-offset arithmetic from the critical path.

title: Game_of_Life optimized via OPEN
text:
Kernel: Game_of_Life (group=all)
Angle applied: OPEN
Speedup: 1.33x (6261 → 4690 cycles)
What changed:
[OPEN-MODE HYPOTHESIS] Avoid the per-generation @block/@unblock churn on the recv tasks: instead of blocking each recv task when it has received all its expected messages and re-unblocking from advance_generation, track expected counts and simply stop processing once the per-direction count is hit (the queue can only deliver the exact number of messages per generation anyway, since each neighbor sends exactly once). This eliminates 4 @block + 4 @unblock builtin calls per generation from the critical path and removes the conditional branches in each recv task that test for the per-direction completion.

title: 7-Point_Stencil optimized via comptime_value_tuning
text:
Kernel: 7-Point_Stencil (group=stencil)
Angle applied: comptime_value_tuning
Speedup: 1.98x (2129 → 1076 cycles)
What changed:
P1: The only change is in the comptime_struct passed to the stencil_3d_7pts module import: the `.BLOCK_SIZE` field was rebound from the host-supplied `BLOCK_SIZE` param to the `MAX_ZDIM` param. No DSDs, tasks, exported symbols, queue/DSR assignments, or function bodies were altered; this is a pure comptime parameter retuning at the `@import_module` / `@concat_structs` site.

P2: Under comptime_value_tuning, raising the stencil's compile-time chunk size to the full vector length collapses the inner blocking loop in `spmv` to a single iteration, eliminating per-chunk loop overhead, DSD re-setup, and communication-pipeline drain/refill between blocks. The 7-point stencil's send/recv DSDs now span the whole z-extent in one shot, cutting `cycles_send` from 2129 to 1076 without changing numerics or host-visible layout.

title: GEMM optimized via comptime_value_tuning
text:
Kernel: GEMM (group=gemm)
Angle applied: comptime_value_tuning
Speedup: 1.04x (51753 → 49573 cycles)
What changed:
P1: The nested fmacs loop in the compute task was reordered: the outer `for (@range(i16, ...))` now iterates over Nt (columns of C) and the inner over Kt, swapping the previous K-outer/N-inner order. The `C_dsd` mem1d_dsd is now built once outside the outer loop and `@increment_dsd_offset`-ed per j; the `A_dsd` mem1d_dsd is reset per j via `@set_dsd_base_addr` and incremented per k. A `jKt = j*Kt` scalar hoists the B index.

P2: Under comptime_value_tuning, swapping the loop nest fixes a single C column across the entire Kt inner sweep, so each `@fmacs` reuses the same `C_dsd` register state and only the A pointer advances per k. The `j*Kt` multiply is hoisted out of the Kt-long inner loop, replacing Kt multiplies with one add-base. Fewer DSD reconstructions and one fewer inner-loop scalar op per fmacs trims the per-iteration cycle count, yielding the ~2180-cycle drop.
